- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-cycle; adjust downward if recent price action shows mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.5 units per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0 unit lag correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often ignores it; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion completes.
